To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
propionate-degrading methanogenic populations are most active in the temperature range of 32 to 43°C and at a pH of 6.8.
The fastest growth of propionotrophic methanogens occurs at pH 6 to 8 and 30 to 45°C, and the fastest growth of acetotrophic methanogenesis occurs at pH 5 to 7 and 30 to45°C.
the fastest growth rates of propionate-oxidizing and acetate-degrading methanogenic cultures occur at pH 7 and 37°C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of methanogenic bacteria from anaerobic digesters, and the characterization of their metabolic capabilities.
the development of enrichment culture techniques for isolating methanogens from natural environments.
the isolation and characterization of the microbial species involved in the methanogenic degradation of propionate and acetate in the rumen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fastest propionate-degrading methanogenic population grew best at pH 7.2 to 7.5, 37 to 40°C, in a medium containing 0.5 g of yeast extract per liter.
methanogenic propionotrophs have an optimum temperature of 37°C and a pH optimum of 7.2 to 7.6.
propionate degradation is fastest in the pH range from 6.8-8.5, at 32-45°C, and in minimal medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fastest growth rates of propionate-degrading populations were achieved at pH 7.0, 40°C, and in complex medium.
the fastest methanogenic growth occurred at 40°C in complex medium with 10 mM propionate at pH 7.0 to 7.5.
methanogens growing on propionate and acetate in enrichment cultures have similar temperature and pH optima but different nutrient requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
methanogenic propionotrophic populations are not as fast-growing as methanogenic acetonotrophic populations.

the conditions for fastest growth of the methanogens and acetogens in propionate-degrading enrichments are quite different from those of the propionotrophs, and this should be considered when designing enrichments and reactors.
